In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the North American and Eurasian plates are moving apart at a rate of 2–3 cm/yr.
the North American –Eurasian plate is moving in a direction approximately north-northwest with a velocity of approximately 2 cm/yr.

the North American – European relative motion is about 2.5 cm/year in a northeasterly direction, and that the North American plate is moving relative to the South American plate at a rate of about 1 cm/year.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to measure plate motions, but that the measurement of plate motions is not a simple task.
the present state of the art is such that we have the techniques, but we need the time.
the North American – European relative motion is about 2.2 cm/year with a 90% probability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a network of zenith tubes is an effective tool for monitoring plate motions, and the results of this study will be useful for the design of future plate motion monitoring programs.
the plate motion estimates obtained by astronomical methods are not significantly different from those derived from geodetic measurements.
the accuracy of the measurements is not a limiting factor, but that the precision of the observations is.
